dedupe_keys.name: emilia romagna italy environmental and economic effects of pay as you throw waste charging

description: This case study evaluates the pay-as-you-throw (PAYT) schemes that link household waste fees to the amount of unsorted waste, using their staggered roll-out across municipalities of Emilia-Romagna, Italy. The authors, at the European Commission's Joint Research Centre, compared two-way fixed effects, staggered and synthetic difference-in-differences methods to deal with uneven adoption and weak parallel trends, and published the work in an open-access journal article. Coverage is the municipalities of one Italian region over the years of the roll-out, with sorted collection rates, waste per capita and service cost components as outcomes. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence and is listed in the JRC publications repository. Caveats: adoption was not random, and the authors find that municipalities selected into PAYT by capacity and performance. The study found a robust increase of about 10 percentage points in sorted collection rates, driven almost entirely by less unsorted waste per person, not more sorted waste, and no significant rise in the total cost of the waste service, though the mix of cost components shifted. Simulation uses: policy effect sizes for waste demand and collection cost models. Related records: the Italian municipal solid waste cost panel (data-italy-municipal-solid-waste-cost-panel) and the Dutch PAYT replication package (data-payt-linked-service-transitions-and-recorded-residual-waste-in-dutch-municipalities-results-replication-packag-p02956) cover related evidence.
